transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~74 minutes
Location: Zoom - internal
Attendees: Avery Chen, Marcus Patel, Sofia Ruiz, Devon Park, Aria Thompson, Ellen Park, Ravi Singh, Maya Lopez, Tom Bennett

Summary:
Quick tabletop wargame simulating a mid-launch spike that triggers model routing thrash and partial KV cache eviction. Walked through detection, fallback, and communications. Focus on rollback vs staged degradation, canary plan for next week.

Topics:
- Detection: symptom triage (increased p95, token drops)
- Fast fallback: model-variant downgrade, regional routing
- Cost/latency tradeoffs during degraded mode
- Runbook gaps: KV warmup, tracing names, SLA sim sheets

Action items: (see metadata list)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: All right folks, thanks for joining, we'll kick off the winter contingency war game. we've got a simulated greenfield launch traffic pattern, and the idea is to exercise our staged degrade and canary rollback. Marcus, you'll run the incident timeline?
[00:22] Marcus Patel: Yep, I'll narrate. so at T+12 minutes we see latency p95 climbing from 220ms to 750ms across us-west-2, some error rates creeping in, and the KV cache eviction rate jumps — oh sorry, the Kv-cache, sometimes the transcript does the lowercase, but eh.
[00:45] Devon Park: Quick clarification, are we assuming the dedicated pool is fully reserved or we're in shared/dedicated hybrid? that changes routing.
[00:53] Avery Chen: For the sim, treat it as Dedicated with burst into hosted. so initial capacity is pinned, then autoscaler fails to catch up because of large sequence tail latencies.
[01:10] Sofia Ruiz: Stakeholder note: Product needs to know whether we prefer model downgrade or region failover as primary fallback — customers care about response correctness more than micro-latency, but enterprise SLAs will push us the other way.
[01:33] Ellen Park: From exec perspective, minimize noisy rollback; degrade gracefully is preferred but must be bounded. we cannot linger in degraded mode for more than 10 minutes without escalation.
[01:47] Marcus Patel: T+18, okay in the sim the routing controller attempts a feed-forward rebalancing and we start seeing token duplication on clients — looks like ephemeral connections re-issuing requests. we need a backoff plus de-dupe at edge.
[02:14] Tom Bennett: Can we tie that to the client SDK version? older SDKs do aggressive retries. let's note that in the runbook.
[02:30] Aria Thompson: Observability gap: current spans don't include model-variant tag consistently, so it's hard to tell which variant suffered. I'll add tracing tag requirements to the runbook.
[02:47] Avery Chen: Good. okay fallback options list: 1) model-variant downgrade to quantized variant (lower perf but lower mem), 2) regional spill to eu-central-1, 3) rate limit more aggressively at edge. pros/cons?
[03:12] Devon Park: Downgrading model variant helps with memory pressure but introduces risk of hallucination — we need a quick eval set to compute quality regress. we don't have a fast path to evaluate quality under load today.
[03:36] Sofia Ruiz: Could we do a shadow verification stream to a canary model and collect sample outputs for regression detection? even if it's delayed, it informs rollback decisions.
[03:58] Marcus Patel: T+30 in the sim, eviction spikes and some pods OOM; autoscaler scales but provisioning delay is too long. fallback executed: we triggered model-variant downgrade and started a regional spill to hosted. latency dropped to 420ms but errors persisted for 4 minutes.
[04:25] Maya Lopez: That 4 minute window is where customers see degraded UX. we need communications plan: internal page and external status page template. who owns the external comm?
[04:42] Ravi Singh: Ops will own external status but PM should sign off on content. I'll draft a template and share.
[04:53] Avery Chen: Note: include suggested wording for staged degradation — we had a previous template in the postmortem but it's out of date. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/templates/status-message (note - may be out of sync).
[05:12] Marcus Patel: Observability sweet spot: add a derived metric 'model_degrade_index' combining p95, kv_eviction_rate, and error_rate. threshold > 0.7 triggers fallback orchestration. but need to calibrate.
[05:33] Devon Park: Also consider KV warmup: cold starts cause tail latency. runbook should include explicit prefix cache warm-up step prior to canary ramp.
[05:48] Aria Thompson: I'll add the warmup script to the runbook and a small job that runs 30m before the canary. link to snippet will be in the doc.
[06:05] Avery Chen: Great. now talk about rollback vs degrade timeboxes. Ellen, you indicated 10 minutes is max for degraded mode before escalation?
[06:16] Ellen Park: yes, 10 minutes unless it's reducing error rate steadily. leadership wants explicit SLO for rollback timeline.
[06:27] Sofia Ruiz: For the next rehearsal we should include a measurable SLA simulation: what token-cost delta and revenue impact is acceptable during degrade. I will coordinate with Finance.
[06:44] Marcus Patel: T+45, decision point — degrade executed, sample outputs show 6% quality drift. another 5 minutes and we decide to rollback. rollback causes spike in latency for first minute while caches repopulate. that's expected.
[07:05] Tom Bennett: Can we smooth rollback with staged fan-in so caches warm without full rollback ripple? maybe route 10% traffic to new variant and ramp.
[07:18] Devon Park: That's the canary ramp pattern, but needs orchestrator support for gradual traffic shifts and KV sticky routing; current orchestrator can do weights but not sticky cache affinity.
[07:38] Marcus Patel: Noted. I'll add an item to evaluate sticky routing or session affinity in orchestrator (see action items).
[07:55] Aria Thompson: Observability play: when we do a staged ramp, make sure we have per-weighted metrics and per-variant histograms. current dashboards aggregate over all variants and hide regressions.
[08:20] Avery Chen: Next, communications and runbook handoff. who's owner of the contingency runbook?
[08:29] Sofia Ruiz: I'll be primary owner with Marcus as SRE reviewer and Aria on observability. Devon on performance sims.
[08:40] Ellen Park: Please include a short checklist for legal/enterprise customers — e.g., KMS/HSM mention, audit log location for any fallback events.
[08:53] Ravi Singh: We'll include a procurement contact and template notice for legal.
[09:05] Marcus Patel: Quick note on private deployments: some of the on-prem customers can't accept automatic regional spillover. runbook should have a gated fallback path for private clusters where we disable cross-customer routing.
[09:26] Devon Park: Good call. add isolation policy reference in the doc.
[09:35] Sofia Ruiz: Action item recap: Marcus - fallback routing policy; Devon - perf sims; Aria - observability tags and dashboards; Sofia - update runbook and status templates. schedule next canary rehearsal for Jan 21 09:00 PST.
[09:58] Tom Bennett: Also, we should run a small blast radius test against a curated subset of customers to validate rollback mechanics. I'll coordinate with Customer Success next week.
[10:12] Avery Chen: Anything else? any low probability-high impact we missed?
[10:19] Marcus Patel: There's a subtle KV eviction race when we combine large batch requests and quantized kernels, leads to small memory fragmentation on certain GPU families. we've seen it in perf lab with A100 gen1 vs gen3. put a note in runbook under kernel compat.
[10:44] Devon Park: Also include a quick checklist to verify quantized model quality for the most critical prompts; call it a litmus set.
[10:58] Maya Lopez: And add steps for a post-incident quality sweep to check model hallucination rates for a seeded prompt list.
[11:12] Avery Chen: Okay wrap up. I'll send the runbook template and action items to the Slack channel and create a follow-up calendar invite for the Jan 21 rehearsal. thanks everyone.
[11:28] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional speaker attribution mix-ups and auto-caption typos (e.g., "KV cache" -> "K V cash") present. References to internal docs are placeholders and will be updated by owners.
